title: Exchange naturality of ordinary finite-twist units
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions] and the signed finite twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Let $v:X'\to X$ be any morphism of $k$-schemes, $p:\mathbf A^1_X\to X$, $p':\mathbf A^1_{X'}\to X'$ the projections [def-sbc-affine-space], and $w=\mathbf A^1_v$. For either topology use the derived adjunctions and ordinary cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For $L=A(r)_X$, $r\in\mathbf Z$, write $\theta:p'^*v^*\cong w^*p^*$ for the inverse-image square identification, and $\beta:v^*Rp_*\to Rp'_*w^*$ for its counit-transpose exchange (on the etale site this is [sbc-def-base-change-map] on the exchanged square). Then
$$Rp'_*(\theta_L^{-1})\circ\beta_{p^*L}\circ v^*(\eta_{p,L})=\eta_{p',v^*L}.$$
For the etale-origin coefficients on the pro-etale site, the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the canonical counit mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] identify this equation and the named exchange maps with their etale counterparts. If the two units in the equation are isomorphisms, the exchange component $\beta_{p^*L}$ is an isomorphism. The ordinary pullback maps satisfy
$$(\mathbf A^1_v)^*p^*=p'^*v^*,$$
and for every finite coefficient morphism $u$ between the specified twists, including changes of finite level and quotient maps,
$$p^*\circ H^q(u)=H^q(p^*u)\circ p^*.$$
These equations hold for all $q\in\mathbf Z$, are identified by the canonical site comparisons, and imply the corresponding equations for inverses whenever the pullback maps are invertible. No invertibility of the units or exchange is assumed in the unconditional equations, and there is no flatness requirement on $u$.

proof.text: Use the canonical signed-twist pullbacks of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The projection square is cartesian by [def-sbc-affine-space]. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$ its projection is $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, so it is affine; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $p$ and its base change $p'$ qcqs. No condition on $v$ is needed. All coefficients used below are sheaves in degree zero, so the bounded-below hypotheses in the site-comparison statements hold.

source.place: Base change on Y: specify the square, coefficient objects and qcqs hypotheses.

proof.text: In either topology apply [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] with $(L_1,R_1)=(p^*,Rp_*)$, $(L_2,R_2)=(p'^*,Rp'_*)$, $G=v^*$, $H=w^*$ and $\alpha=\theta$. Its right mate is the specified $\beta$: [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives transpose $w^*\varepsilon_p\circ\theta_{Rp_*}$, precisely the inverse-image description in [sbc-def-base-change-map] on the exchanged etale square; the pro-etale exchange is defined by that same transpose. The cited unit equation is $\beta_{p^*L}v^*\eta_{p,L}=Rp'_*(\theta_L)\eta_{p',v^*L}$. Compose with $Rp'_*(\theta_L^{-1})$; functoriality cancels $\theta_L^{-1}\theta_L$ and gives the required equation. This argument uses no invertibility of either unit or of $\beta$.

source.place: Base change on Y: compatibility of exchange with the units; right-mate normalization of Stacks Tag 0B65 (categories.tex, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints).

proof.text: Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ and $a_u:C_Uu_e^*\cong u_p^*C_V$ for [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For $u=p,p'$, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] defines $b_u:C_VRu_{e,*}\to Ru_{p,*}C_U$ as the right mate of $a_u^{-1}$. Apply [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] to this square and cancel $Ru_{p,*}(a_{u,M}^{-1})$: this gives $\eta^p_{u,C_VM}=Ru_{p,*}(a_{u,M})\,b_{u,u_e^*M}\,C_V(\eta^e_{u,M})$. Thus these are the named units under comparison. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] with $(f,f',g,g')=(p,p',v,w)$ and input $p_e^*L$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1; its $S,T$ identify the named etale and pro-etale exchange components. The square coherence in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$. Substituting these unit, exchange and square identifications in step 2 identifies its entire equation on the two sites. No comparison for $Rv_*$ or $Rw_*$ is invoked.

source.place: Base change on Y: canonical site transport; compare main-20261015 lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange.proof.md and Stacks Tag 0B65.

proof.text: Use [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] to identify module-derived sections with ordinary abelian-sheaf cohomology, compatibly with geometric pullback. Apply the composition clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] to the geometric site morphisms for $(p,w)$ and $(v,p')$, evaluating at the final object. Since $p\circ w=v\circ p'$, it gives $w^*p^*=p'^*v^*$ after the canonical inverse-image square identification, in each topology, for $q\ge0$. For a finite coefficient morphism $u:L\to L'$ use clause (2), applied to the underlying abelian sheaves, to get $p^*H^q(u)=H^q(p^*u)p^*$. Changes of level and quotient maps are such sheaf morphisms; the canonical twist pullbacks in step 1 identify their pulled-back coefficients. This applies a cohomology functor to a morphism, not an exactness assertion for tensoring with a quotient. Thus no flatness assumption on $u$ occurs. The units themselves are natural in any such fixed-ring sheaf morphism because a unit is a natural transformation.

source.place: Base change on Y and Coefficients: ordinary pullback composition and coefficient naturality; Stacks Tags 01F8 (cohomology.tex, lemma-functoriality), 01FB (remark-explain-arrow), site form stated by the cited node.

proof.text: The global comparison $c_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology] is explicitly derived sections of the comparison unit followed by final-object evaluation. It is therefore the cohomological pullback along $\nu_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback]. Apply its composition clause to the two paths around the comparison square for any scheme morphism $u:U\to V$. Using $a_u$ from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], the result is $c_Uu_e^*=H^q(a_u^{-1})u_p^*c_V$. Its coefficient naturality clause also gives $c_TH^q(h)=H^q(\nu_T^*h)c_T$ for every coefficient map $h$. These two equations identify all the ordinary equations in step 4 across the sites. For coefficients at different finite levels one can regard both as modules over a common $\mathbf Z/\ell^N$ annihilating them; their maps are linear there, so this is still the natural finite-ring comparison. For $q<0$, a sheaf has an injective resolution concentrated in nonnegative degrees in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; its sections complex has no negative terms. Thus its negative cohomology is zero and the equations hold uniquely as equations of zero-group maps.

source.place: Base change on Y and Coefficients: identify ordinary equations using the comparison unit, final-object evaluation and pullback composition.

proof.text: If the two units are invertible, step 2 rewrites the exchange component as $\beta_{p^*L}=Rp'_*(\theta_L)\eta_{p',v^*L}(v^*\eta_{p,L})^{-1}$, a composite of isomorphisms. Finally, a commuting square $bP=P'a$ with $P,P'$ invertible gives $P'^{-1}b=aP^{-1}$ by multiplying on the left and right by their inverses. Apply this to each pullback naturality square and to its site comparison. This proves the asserted inverse equations under exactly their stated conditional hypotheses. Identity base maps, zero coefficient maps and empty schemes require no change in these formal equations.
